title: Maine's 1st Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: The 2026 general election for Maine's 1st Congressional District pits Democratic incumbent Chellie Pingree against Republican nominee Ronald Russell. Pingree, first elected in 2008 and seeking a tenth term, has won re-election by comfortable margins in a district that includes Portland and the southern coastal region of Maine. The Republican primary concluded on June 9, 2026, with Russell defeating Joshua Pietrowicz by a 53.7% to 46.3% margin. The district is rated as Safe/Solid Democratic by major nonpartisan election forecasters, though Russell's background as a West Point graduate, Army veteran, and defense contractor gives Republicans a standard-bearer with a compelling biography.
polling_note: No public general election polls were found for the Pingree-Russell matchup as of mid-2026. The most recent primary poll from the University of New Hampshire (May 21-25, 2026) showed 68% of Republican primary voters undecided, with Russell at 24% and Pietrowicz at 7%.

candidates.name: Chellie Pingree
candidates.summary: Chellie Pingree is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Maine's 1st Congressional District, first elected in 2008. She previously served in the Maine Senate from 1992 to 2000, including four years as Majority Leader, and was President and CEO of Common Cause from 2003 to 2006. Pingree sits on the House Appropriations Committee and has focused on issues including prescription drug pricing, land conservation, and government transparency.

candidates.name: Ronald Russell
candidates.summary: Ronald Russell is a Republican candidate and retired U.S. Army Colonel who won the June 9, 2026 Republican primary for Maine's 1st Congressional District. A West Point graduate and a 30-year Army veteran who served as an Airborne Ranger and Green Beret, he later co-founded the defense contractor Far Ridgeline Engagements in North Carolina. Russell was also the Republican nominee for this seat in 2024, losing to incumbent Chellie Pingree, and is making a second bid for the office.

forecast.rationale: No public general-election polls are available for this race (based_on_poll_count=0), so the forecast relies entirely on fundamentals. Democratic incumbent Chellie Pingree has represented Maine's 1st District since 2008, seeking a tenth term, and has consistently won re-election by comfortable margins in a district encompassing Portland and the southern Maine coast — an area that leans Democratic. Major nonpartisan election forecasters rate this seat Safe/Solid Democratic. Republican nominee Ronald Russell is a credible challenger (West Point graduate, Army veteran, defeated an opponent 53.7%–46.3% in the June 9 primary), but he lost to Pingree in 2024 and faces a long-tenured incumbent in a district with a strong Democratic lean. Without any general-election polling or indicators of a shift in competitiveness, the fundamentals point to an overwhelming Democratic advantage. Confidence is medium rather than high due to the complete absence of general-election polling, introducing greater uncertainty about the current state of the race.
